# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 15 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_015_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 7

**1** "Why was she an old woman before and now she's young?" I asked. **2** "I'll explain," she said. "She appeared as an old woman in the first two visions because your spirit was old and tired — already fading — with no strength left, worn down by your doubts and failures. **3** Think of an elderly person who has given up hope of ever feeling young again — they don't look forward to anything; they're just waiting to die. That was you, Hermas. You were exhausted by life's worries, you had given up on yourselves, and the Lord's renewal wasn't reaching you. But then he spoke to you through her, and you turned back to him — and the renewal came. Your weakness left. Strength returned. You became young again. **4** And when you see the tower become a single stone — that too will happen. All who have believed wholeheartedly will be joined into one: one body, one mind, one spirit, one faith, one love. When that day comes, the tower will be complete and everyone will celebrate." **5** "One more question," I said. "Why do the stones from the sea fit together with the stones from dry land?" **6** "Because they all heard and believed," she said. "The sea-stones went through fire to get there — they were tested and purified. The land-stones didn't need that kind of testing."

---

*PNEUMA note: The sea-stones tested by fire = martyrs; land-stones not needing fire = those whose holy life was sufficient. Both kinds of faithfulness are honored equally in the building.*
